title: Setting Up and Solving for One Unknown Parameter

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, 3^2)$. Given that $\text{P}(X < 18) = 0.10$, find $\mu$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, 5^2)$. Given that $\text{P}(X < 74) = 0.80$, find $\mu$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(80, \sigma^2)$. Given that $\text{P}(X > 92) = 0.10$, find $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The random variable $Y$ has distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(50, \sigma^2)$. Given that $\text{P}(Y < 41) = 0.15$, find $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: Repair times $T$ hours for a machine satisfy $T \sim \text{N}(\mu, 0.4^2)$. It is found that 95% of repairs take longer than 1.1 hours. Find $\mu$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: In a sample of 2500 observations from a normal distribution with mean 50 and standard deviation $\sigma$, exactly 100 observations exceed 62. Find the estimate of $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The lengths $L$ cm of metal rods produced by a machine satisfy $L \sim \text{N}(\mu, 1.5^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that $\text{P}(L < 24.2) = 0.85$, find $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given instead that $\text{P}(L > 21.0) = 0.90$, find $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The lifetimes $T$ hours of light bulbs are normally distributed with mean 1200 hours and standard deviation $\sigma$ hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that 10% of the light bulbs fail before 1050 hours, find the value of $\sigma$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using this value of $\sigma = 117.0$, find the proportion of light bulbs that last longer than 1350 hours.

questions.text: Package masses $X$ grams sent by a postal service are modelled by $\text{N}(120, \sigma^2)$. In a random sample of 600 packages, exactly 72 have mass exceeding 134 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Estimate the probability $\text{P}(X > 134)$, and find the corresponding standard normal value $z$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence estimate the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The mass $X$ kg of adult sheep in a flock satisfies a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 0.2\mu$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that $\text{P}(X < 72.0) = 0.75$, find the value of $\mu$ and hence find $\sigma$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using $\mu = 63.45$ and $\sigma = 12.69$, find the probability that a randomly chosen sheep has mass between 55.0 kg and 75.0 kg.

questions.text: The volume $V$ ml of drink dispensed into cups by a vending machine satisfies $V \sim \text{N}(\mu, 12.0^2)$. Cups with less than 220 ml overflow or are underfilled.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The machine is calibrated so that only 2.5% of cups contain less than 220 ml. Find the setting for $\mu$, giving your answer to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: With this mean $\mu = 243.5$ ml, find the probability that a randomly selected cup contains more than 260 ml.

questions.text: The journey times $T$ minutes for commuters on an express train satisfy $T \sim \text{N}(42.0, \sigma^2)$. Commuters are eligible for compensation if their journey time exceeds 50.0 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a survey of 400 journeys, 32 commuters were eligible for compensation. Estimate $\text{P}(T > 50.0)$ and hence find $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using $\sigma = 5.69$, find the journey time $t$ that is exceeded by exactly 1% of journeys, giving your answer to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In a random sample of 8 journeys, find the probability that at least one journey qualifies for compensation, using $\text{P}(T > 50.0) = 0.080$.

questions.text: The breaking force $F$ newtons of synthetic fibres is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. Fibres are classified as Defective if $F < 140.0$, Standard if $140.0 \le F < 190.0$, and Premium if $F \ge 190.0$. It is known that the standard deviation is $\sigma = 18.0$ newtons.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that 6.7% of fibres are Defective, find the mean breaking force $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using $\mu = 167.0$, find the proportion of fibres classified as Premium.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In a test of 5 randomly chosen fibres, find the probability that exactly 2 fibres are Premium.
